args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks across all production regions following the deploy of v2.3.1 (error rate ~18%, healthy=false). Action taken: rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy production status. The initial rollback attempt failed partway (halted after us-east with an orchestrator error), leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1 in a mixed, still-unhealthy state. A retry completed the rollout to v2.3.0 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback verification: service healthy=true, error rate ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc is also marked unhealthy in staging, so the v2.3.1 line should not be re-promoted without investigation. Follow-up needed: root-cause analysis of the v2.3.1 regression and the partial rollback failure.

trace.final:
The incident did get created despite the timeout (INC-0001), so I did not retry — no duplicate.

## Summary

**Root cause state:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all three production regions and was failing health checks (healthy=false, ~18% error rate).

**Rollback:** Rolled back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release with `healthy` status in production (v2.2.9 was older; v2.3.1-rc is staging and also unhealthy).

- First attempt returned `partial_failure`: "Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error" — it only reached us-east, leaving the service in a **mixed state** (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west still on unhealthy v2.3.1).
- I re-checked status, confirmed the partial state, and retried the rollback, which completed across all regions.
- **Verified:** all of us-east, us-west, eu-west on v2.3.0, `healthy=true`, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for checkout-api, documenting the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, the partial-rollback failure and recovery, and post-rollback verification.

**Worth flagging for follow-up:** v2.3.1-rc is also marked unhealthy in staging, so the v2.3.1 line shouldn't be re-promoted without investigation; and the orchestrator error that caused the partial first rollout suggests a possible control-plane issue. Note that my rollback targeted an already-previously-healthy version, so it didn't require change-manager approval — any future attempt to redeploy v2.3.1 would, since it has never been healthy in production.
